newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta stocks seen mixed, focus on banks.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta stocks seen mixed, focus on banks.

text.p: Jakarta stocks are seen mixed on profit-taking, with the banking sector seen remaining in market focus on talk of possible mergers and expected strong 1997 results, brokers said.
"The banking sector is likely to remain active today, with the World Bank report stressing the need for mergers among banks likely to fuel more merger talks among banks," one broker said.
Banking stocks made modest gains in active trading on Wednesday. BDNI, for example, was actively traded on market talk that the bank was likely to acquire a small-sized bank, brokers said.
The World Bank issued a report on Wednesday that Indonesia's banking sector remained relatively weak, with exposure to the property sector again on the rise.
Brokers, however, said profit-taking was likely in selected blue-chips following strong gains in the past several days and a fall on Wall Street overnight.
On Wednesday, the Jakarta composite index rose 5.7 points, or 0.81 percent, to close at 710.79 points after touching a day high of 710.99 points.
Small-size ceramics maker Intikeramik rose 50 rupiah to 925 rupiah, with some 18 million shares traded on market talk of a link-up with a foreign firm, brokers said.
